prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer first
- There’s no single “best” platform — pick the one that matches the kind of trip you want:
  - Airbnb: best for unique places, local hosts, flexible stay types (private rooms, shared, entire homes), lots of filters and experience-type listings.
  - Vrbo: focused on entire homes / family stays (vacation rentals) — fewer shared rooms, often good for families/groups wanting full houses.
  - Booking.com: best if you want instant bookings, a mix of hotels + apartments, often easier free-cancellation options and last‑minute availability; less emphasis on host interaction.

How to choose between them (quick criteria)
- If you want a whole home and family-friendly filters → Vrbo.
- If you want a unique listing or local-host experience → Airbnb.
- If you want flexibility, hotels + apartments, pay-at-arrival options or frequent last-minute deals → Booking.com.
- Also check total price (including cleaning, service, city taxes) and cancellation policy — they vary a lot between platforms/listings.

How to find a good host — practical checklist
1. Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months)
   - Look for multiple, recent positive stays. Pay attention to comments about communication, cleanliness, check-in, and accuracy of listing.
2. Prefer verified/top hosts
   - Airbnb “Superhost” / Vrbo “Premier Host” / Booking.com “Top Rated” tags indicate consistently good reviews and responsiveness.
3. Check response rate and response time
   - Fast, reliable replies before booking are a good sign. Many platforms show response rate/time.
4. Inspect review details, not just star ratings
   - Guests often mention specific issues (noise, cleanliness, hidden fees, check-in problems) — weigh those more than generic praise.
5. Look for consistency between photos, calendar, and description
   - Listings that have up-to-date photos and a filled-out calendar show professionalism.
6. Check house rules and policies
   - Make sure policies (guests allowed, pets, smoking, check-in/out) match your needs. Hard or unusual rules can be a red flag.
7. Ask questions before booking
   - Ask about check-in details, parking, Wi‑Fi speed, neighborhood safety, heating/AC, and anything specific to your needs.
8. Watch for red flags
   - No recent reviews, evasive answers, pressure to move off-platform payment, inconsistent photos or vague descriptions, host cancels frequently.
9. Use platform protections
   - Book and pay inside the platform so you have recourse for refunds, claims, or platform support.
10. Consider a short message/phone call
   - A short video/phone chat can build trust if you’re booking a pricey or long stay.

Pre-booking message template (short)
- Hi [Host name], I’m [first name] traveling with [number of guests, relationship]. We arrive [date/time], plan to stay [purpose — vacation/work]. Is the place available and is self check-in possible? Also, is street parking available? Thanks!
- Use this to test response time and helpfulness.

What to check on the listing page
- Total price breakdown (cleaning fee, service fee, taxes)
- Cancellation policy and refund windows
- Check-in instructions and key exchange / self check-in availability
- Essential amenities (Wi‑Fi, heating/AC, washer/dryer, kitchen basics)
- Exact location (neighborhood, proximity to transport/attractions)

Booking & safety tips
- Keep all communication and payment on platform.
- Use a credit card for extra chargeback protection.
- Photograph the property on arrival to document any pre-existing damage.
- If host cancels last minute or listing is misrepresented, contact platform support immediately; consider travel insurance for cancellations/interruptions.
- For longer stays, ask about discounts and cleaning schedules.

When something goes wrong
- Message the host first with clear photos and a requested resolution.
- If not resolved quickly, escalate to the platform with evidence (screenshots, photos, messages).
- Check cancellation windows and your rights under the platform’s guest guarantee.

Quick recommendation based on typical trip types
- Solo traveler/short stay/unique stay → Airbnb.
- Family or group needing whole-house and kid‑friendly features → Vrbo.
- Want hotels + apartments, last-minute or free cancellation flexibility → Booking.com.

If you tell me: destination, travel dates, party size and priorities (budget, whole house, location, kid/pet friendly, work/Wi‑Fi needs), I can suggest which platform to prioritize and give wording for messages to specific hosts.
